pages.ja:
時刻は朝の七時過ぎ。
いつもより遅くなってしまったが、この時間なら急がなくとも間に合うだろう。

pages.en:
It is a little after seven in the morning.

I am running later than usual, but at this hour I should make it without having to hurry.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It’s past seven o’clock.
It’s later than usual, but I should still make it on time without hurrying.

pages.ja:
七時四十分。
余裕を持って正門を通り抜け、校舎へ向かう途中。
「
」
何かおかしな違和感に襲われて、足を止めた。
pages.jaRuby:

「
」

pages.en:
Seven forty.

I pass through the front gate with time to spare and start toward the school building.

“————”

A strange sense of wrongness washes over me, bringing me to a halt.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It’s 7:40.
I go through the gate, and as I make my way to the school building…
“
”
I feel something strange and stop.

pages.ja: 「……なんだ？ 別に何がおかしいってワケじゃないよな……」
pages.jaRuby: 「……なんだ？ 別に何がおかしいってワケじゃないよな……」
pages.en: “…What is it? Nothing actually looks wrong…”
pages.mirrorMoon: “…What is this? It’s not like something’s strange, right…?”

pages.ja:
誰かに見られているというワケでもないし、いつもと景色が違うワケでもない。
しいて言うのなら、そう
なんとなく活気がない、というか。
それは校舎に向かう生徒たちだけでなく、木々や校舎そのものも、どこか色あせて見えるような錯覚だった。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
No one is watching me, and the scenery is no different from usual.

If I had to name it, I would say the place somehow lacks vitality.

And it is not only the students walking toward the building. The trees and even the school itself seem strangely faded, as though some of their color has been drained away.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It’s not like someone’s watching me or that something looks different.
If anything, it’s that it’s not that lively.
It feels like the students, and even the trees and the buildings, are dull in color.

pages.ja:
「……気のせいかな。色々あって過敏になってるのかもしれない」
目を瞑って、ポキポキと肩を鳴らす。
……が。
そうやって一呼吸おいて見ても、正体の判らない違和感は消えてはくれなかった。
pages.jaRuby:
「……気のせいかな。色々あって過敏になってるのかもしれない」

pages.en:
“…Maybe it’s my imagination. After everything that’s happened, I might just be on edge.”

I close my eyes and roll my shoulders until they crack.

…But even after taking a moment to collect myself, the nameless unease refuses to fade.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I bet it’s just me. I’m sure that I’m stressed out from all the events that have been happening.”
I close my eyes and rotate my shoulders.
…But.
The strange feeling doesn’t disappear even after that.

pages.ja:
三階に上がって教室に向かう。
と。
ばったり、遠坂と顔を合わせた。
pages.jaRuby:
三階に上がって教室に向かう。
と。
ばったり、遠坂と顔を合わせた。
pages.en:
I climb to the third floor and head toward my classroom.

Then—

I run straight into Tohsaka.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I get up to the third floor and head to my classroom.
Then.
I run into Tohsaka.

pages.ja:
「よっ」
一応、もう顔見知りなワケだし軽く挨拶をする。
「
」
が、遠坂は幽霊でも見たかのように固まっていた。
pages.jaRuby:
「よっ」

「
」
が、遠坂は幽霊でも見たかのように固まっていた。
pages.en:
“Morning.”

We know each other now, after a fashion, so I offer her a casual greeting.

“———————”

But Tohsaka freezes as though she has seen a ghost.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Yo.”
I know her, so I greet her.
“
”
But Tohsaka freezes as if she’s seen a ghost.

pages.ja:
「遠坂？ なんだよ、顔になんかついてるのか？」
制服の裾で頬を拭ってみる。
「
」
遠坂はそれでも口を開けず、
ふん、と顔を背けて自分の教室へと戻っていった。
pages.jaRuby:
「遠坂？ なんだよ、顔になんかついてるのか？」

」

ふん、と顔を背けて自分の教室へと戻っていった。
pages.en:
“Tohsaka? What is it? Is there something on my face?”

I scrub at my cheek with the cuff of my uniform.

“———————”

Still without a word, Tohsaka turns away with a huff and retreats to her classroom.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Tohsaka? What? Is there something on my face?”
I wipe my cheek with my uniform.
“
”
But Tohsaka doesn’t even reply.
She looks away from me and goes back to her classroom.

pages.ja:
「…………？？？？」
なんだろう、今のリアクションは。
遠坂のやつ、挨拶をされたら無視できる性格じゃないと思うんだけど。
pages.jaRuby:
「…………？？？？」
なんだろう、今のリアクションは。
遠坂のやつ、挨拶をされたら無視できる性格じゃないと思うんだけど。
pages.en:
“…………????”

What was that reaction supposed to mean?

Tohsaka does not strike me as the sort of person who could simply ignore someone who greeted her.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“……????”
What was that?
I don’t think it’s like her to ignore someone who greeted her.

pages.ja:
「
」
教室に入るなり、またあの違和感があった。
誰かが菓子でも持ち込んだのか、微かに甘い匂いがする。
pages.jaRuby:
「
」

誰かが菓子でも持ち込んだのか、微かに甘い匂いがする。
pages.en:
“————”

The moment I enter the classroom, that same unease returns.

There is a faintly sweet smell in the air, as though someone brought in candy.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
”
The strange feeling hits me again when I go into my classroom.
Someone might’ve brought snacks in here, as I smell a slight sweetness in the air.

pages.ja:
「……別に、いつも通りの教室だよな」
男連中に挨拶をしながら席に着く。
ホームルームが始まるまであと十分ほど。
その間にぐるりと教室を見渡して、鞄のない席に気が付いた。
pages.jaRuby:
「……別に、いつも通りの教室だよな」

その間にぐるりと教室を見渡して、鞄のない席に気が付いた。
pages.en:
“…It looks exactly like the classroom always does.”

I exchange greetings with the other boys and take my seat.

There are about ten minutes left before homeroom. I use them to survey the room, and notice one desk without a schoolbag beside it.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…The classroom’s like always.”
I head to my seat while greeting the guys.
There are about ten more minutes until homeroom starts.
I look around the room, and I notice a seat without a bag.

pages.ja:
「慎二のヤツ、欠席か」
そういえば昨日も部活を休んでいたっけ。
ああ見えても慎二は几帳面で、神経質なまでに規則を守ろうとするヤツだ。
そんなあいつが二日も学校にいないというのは、なんとなく気になった。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“So Shinji’s absent.”

Come to think of it, he missed club practice yesterday too.

For all his faults, Shinji is meticulous, almost neurotic about obeying rules.

The fact that he has missed two days of school bothers me more than it should.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Shinji’s absent, huh?”
Come to think of it, he wasn’t at the club yesterday either.
Shinji is actually quite punctual and he tries hard to follow the rules.
It worries me a bit that a guy like him has been absent for two days.

pages.ja:
昼休みになった。
弁当を作ってきた日は大抵、こうして生徒会室に移動する。
何故かというと、教室で弁当を広げると男どもにはハシをつつかれ、女どもには茶化されるからである。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
Lunch break arrives.

Whenever I bring a homemade lunch, I generally come here to the student council room.

If I open it in the classroom, the boys steal food with their chopsticks and the girls never stop teasing me.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It’s lunchtime.
I usually go to the student council room when I make my own lunch.
It’s because the guys will take my food and the girls will make fun of me if I eat in the classroom.

pages.ja:
「なんだ一成。おまえ、昼は食べないのか」
「ああ、先ほど済ませた。今はともかく眠くてな、昼休みが終わる前に起こしてくれ」
べったりと机に伏したまま、一成はそんな事を言う。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“What’s wrong, Issei? Aren’t you having lunch?”

“I ate a short while ago. At present, I am simply very sleepy. Wake me before lunch break ends.”

Issei delivers this instruction without lifting his face from the desk.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“What’s wrong, Issei? You’re not eating lunch?”
“No, I just finished eating. I’m just really sleepy right now. Wake me up when lunch is over.”
Issei then puts his head on the table.

pages.ja:
「なんだ、徹夜でもしたのか？ お山じゃ十一時には絶対就寝じゃなかったっけ？」
「うむ……そうなのだが、最近寝付きが良くない。いくら眠っても疲れが取れなくてな。おかげで、ここ数日は暇さえあれば眠っている」
pages.jaRuby:
「なんだ、徹夜でもしたのか？ お山じゃ十一時には絶対就寝じゃなかったっけ？」

pages.en:
“What, were you up all night? I thought lights-out at the temple was always eleven sharp.”

“Mm… It is, but I have not been sleeping well of late. However long I sleep, the fatigue never leaves me. For the past several days, I have spent every spare moment asleep.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Did you stay up all night or something? I thought you had to go to bed at eleven at the temple.”
“Yes… But I’m having difficulty sleeping lately. My fatigue won’t go away no matter how much I sleep. So for the past few days, I’ve been sleeping whenever I get the chance.”

pages.ja:
「……？ なんだそりゃ。暇さえあれば眠ってるんなら、眠気なんてないだろ」
「うぅ、そうなのだがな。いくら眠っても疲れがとれない故、疲れをとる為に眠らざるを得ないのだ。
……矛盾していると分かってはいるのだが、眠いものは仕方がない」
pages.jaRuby:
「……？ なんだそりゃ。暇さえあれば眠ってるんなら、眠気なんてないだろ」
「うぅ、そうなのだがな。いくら眠っても疲れがとれない故、疲れをとる為に眠らざるを得ないのだ。
……矛盾していると分かってはいるのだが、眠いものは仕方がない」
pages.en:
“…? How does that work? If you sleep whenever you get a chance, you shouldn’t still be tired.”

“Ugh, yes, I know. Yet no amount of sleep dispels my fatigue, and so I am forced to sleep in the hope of recovering from it.

“…I realize the contradiction, but when one is sleepy, one is sleepy.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“……? What is that? You shouldn’t be sleepy if you’re sleeping every time you get the chance.”
“That’s true. But sleep won’t let me rest, so I have to sleep to rest.
…I know I’m contradicting myself, but I can’t help feeling sleepy.”

pages.ja:
「
はあ。春にはまだ早いんだけどな、一成」
「春眠暁を覚えずか。まことに耳が痛い」
一成は机につっぷしたまま起きようともしない。
……仕方ない。
重症のようだし、昼休みが終わるまで付き合うとするか

“—Right. Bit early for spring fever, Issei.”

“‘Spring sleep knows no dawn,’ as they say. You have me there.”

Issei remains sprawled across the desk without the slightest intention of rising.

…He seems to have a serious case of it. I may as well keep him company until lunch break ends——
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
Man, it’s too early to be spring, you know?”
“In spring one sleeps a sleep that knows no dawn, huh? You certainly got me there.”
Issei doesn’t even try to get up.
…I guess it can’t be helped.
It looks serious, so I’ll stay here until lunch is over

「

」

Issei rises at an unhurried pace and opens the door.

“Ryuudou. Concerning this morning’s incident in the archery club——”

Kuzuki notices me in the student council room and falls silent.

Souichirou Kuzuki is the homeroom teacher of Class 2-A as well as the student council adviser. He is the strictest teacher in the school and utterly devoid of charm.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Issei gets up slowly and opens the door.
“Ryuudou. It is about the archery club this morning
”
Kuzuki-sensei stops his words after seeing that I’m here.

pages.ja:
「え……？ それじゃ家にも帰ってないんですか？」
「そのようだ。おそらく刑事事件になるだろう。解っているだろうが、無闇に話す事は避けるように」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“What…? Then she hasn’t returned home either?”

“It would appear not. This will most likely become a criminal matter. You understand, I trust, that you are not to discuss it indiscriminately.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Huh…? Then she didn’t even go home?”
“Correct. We will probably call the police. I believe you know, but do not spread the rumor.”

pages.ja:
「

「それに関しても同じだ。間桐慎二も無断欠席しており、家も留守だそうだ。妹である間桐桜は藤村先生の家に泊まっていたというし、事情は知らされていない」

“—I understand that. But in that case, what has become of Matou? A first-year member of the archery club said he met her yesterday, did she not?”

“The same applies to him. Shinji Matou is absent without notice, and his house is reportedly empty. His sister, Sakura Matou, stayed at Ms. Fujimura's home last night and has been told nothing of the circumstances.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
I know. Then how about Matou? The student in the archery club said he saw her and Matou together.”
“It is the same for him as well. Matou Shinji is absent today and his house is empty. His sister, Matou Sakura, was staying over at Fujimura-sensei’s house last night, so she does not know anything.”

pages.ja:
……一成と葛木は、なにやら物騒な会話をしていた。
聞こえてしまった内容を吟味すると、昨日から行方不明の生徒がいて、その生徒と最後に会っていたのが慎二だという事だが

…Issei and Kuzuki are discussing something deeply alarming.

Piecing together what I have overheard, a student has been missing since yesterday, and Shinji was the last person seen speaking to her——
pages.mirrorMoon:
…Issei and Kuzuki are talking about disturbing stuff.
Summing up what they said, it seems that a student’s been missing since last night, and Shinji’s the last one to talk to that student

「邪魔をしたな。そういった事情もある。また下校時間が早まるだろう」
用件だけ述べて、葛木は生徒会室から去っていった。

“Forgive the interruption. Those are the circumstances. Dismissal will likely be moved forward again today.”

Having said all he came to say, Kuzuki leaves the student council room.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Sorry to interrupt. I am sure the school’s curfew will be set at an earlier time now.”
Quickly stating his business, Kuzuki leaves the student council room.

pages.ja:
「……まったく。なあ衛宮、おまえ慎二を見なかったか？」
「いや、見てない。今朝は弓道場にも行かなかったし、あいつが休んでるコトはおまえも知ってるだろ」
「そうか。それならいいんだが……」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“…Honestly. Emiya, have you seen Shinji?”

“No. I didn’t go by the archery range this morning, and you already know he’s absent.”

“I see. If not, then never mind…”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Geez. Have you seen Shinji, Emiya?”
“No. I didn’t go to the archery club this morning. You should know as well that he’s absent, right?”
“I see. I hope that’s the case…”

pages.ja:
深刻そうに顔を曇らせる一成。
まいったな。
そう無遠慮に訊ける話じゃなさそうだが、どうも事は弓道部に関わる事のようだ。
一成には悪いが、無理にでも詳しい話を聞くべきだろう。

pages.en:
Issei’s face clouds over.

—This is bad.

It does not sound like something I can ask about casually, but it clearly concerns the archery club.

I feel bad pressing Issei, but I need to hear the full story.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Issei’s face clouds up.

It’s not something I should rudely butt in on, but it seems this concerns the archery club.
I’m sorry for Issei, but I should get some information out of him.

「ん……？ そうだな、衛宮も部外者という訳ではないし、知っておいてもいいだろう」

「ん……？ そうだな、衛宮も部外者という訳ではないし、知っておいてもいいだろう」
pages.en:
“Issei. You said someone hasn’t been home since yesterday. Who were you talking about? I understand that no one can reach Shinji either, but—”

“Hm…? Yes, I suppose you are not entirely an outsider. You may as well know.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Issei. Who is this person that hasn’t been home? Well, I already know Shinji hasn’t been home.”
“Hm…? Well, you’re no outsider, so I guess you can know.”

pages.ja:
「昨日の夜の話だ。
弓道部の練習に出た娘が帰ってこない、という連絡があってな。至急、練習に参加した生徒たちに話を聞いたところ、行方不明になった生徒と最後に話していたのは慎二だと判ったのだ」
「
」
慎二と、話していた……？
pages.jaRuby:
「昨日の夜の話だ。
弓道部の練習に出た娘が帰ってこない、という連絡があってな。至急、練習に参加した生徒たちに話を聞いたところ、行方不明になった生徒と最後に話していたのは慎二だと判ったのだ」
「
」
慎二と、話していた……？
pages.en:
“It happened last night.

“We received word that a girl who had attended archery practice had not returned home. We immediately questioned the students who had been at practice, and learned that Shinji was the last person seen speaking with the missing student.”

“————”

Speaking with Shinji…?
pages.mirrorMoon:
“It all happened last night.
We got a contact from a family saying that their daughter had yet to come home from the archery club. When we contacted the students who actually went to the club, we found out it was Shinji that last talked to this student.”
“
”
Talked to Shinji…?

pages.ja:
「ちょっと待った。慎二は昨日の練習にはいなかったぞ。
それに、弓道部のみんなとはちゃんと校門で別れたんだが」
pages.jaRuby:
「ちょっと待った。慎二は昨日の練習にはいなかったぞ。
それに、弓道部のみんなとはちゃんと校門で別れたんだが」
pages.en:
“Wait. Shinji wasn’t at practice yesterday.

“Besides, I saw everyone from the archery club leave at the school gates.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hold on. Shinji wasn’t at the practice yesterday.
And I parted with everyone at the school gate.”

pages.ja: 「ああ、衛宮もいたらしいな。話はその後だ。忘れ物をした一年生が戻った時、慎二が道場の前にいたらしい。その時にな、慎二とそいつが口喧嘩をしてたそうなんだ」
pages.jaRuby: 「ああ、衛宮もいたらしいな。話はその後だ。忘れ物をした一年生が戻った時、慎二が道場の前にいたらしい。その時にな、慎二とそいつが口喧嘩をしてたそうなんだ」
pages.en: “Yes, I heard you were there as well. This happened afterward. A first-year student returned for something she had forgotten and saw Shinji standing outside the archery hall. Apparently, he and the missing student were arguing.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Yes, it seems you were there as well. But this is after that. When a student returned to school to get something he forgot, he saw Shinji in front of the archery range. It seems the missing student and Shinji were having a quarrel.”

pages.ja:
「
」
嫌な予感がする。
……あの時、道場に残っている可能性があるとしたら、それは一人しかいないからだ。
pages.jaRuby:
「
」
嫌な予感がする。
……あの時、道場に残っている可能性があるとしたら、それは一人しかいないからだ。
pages.en:
“————”

A terrible suspicion takes hold of me.

…At that hour, there was only one person who might still have been at the archery hall.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
”
I have a bad feeling about this.
…There’s only one student that could’ve been there.

pages.ja: 「一成、肝心な話をぼかすな。……それで、昨日から行方不明になってる生徒ってのは誰なんだ」
pages.jaRuby: 「一成、肝心な話をぼかすな。……それで、昨日から行方不明になってる生徒ってのは誰なんだ」
pages.en: “Issei, stop dancing around it. …Who is the student that’s been missing since yesterday?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Don’t leave out the important detail, Issei. Who is this student that’s been missing?”

pages.ja:
「……うむ。美綴綾子、弓道部の主将だ。
彼女は道場の鍵を職員室に戻した後、弓道場前で見かけられてから一向に行方が知れない」
一成は言いづらそうに、視線を逸らしながらそう言った。
pages.jaRuby:
「……うむ。美綴綾子、弓道部の主将だ。
彼女は道場の鍵を職員室に戻した後、弓道場前で見かけられてから一向に行方が知れない」
一成は言いづらそうに、視線を逸らしながらそう言った。
pages.en:
“...Ayako Mitsuzuri, captain of the archery club.

“After returning the key to the archery hall at the faculty office, she was seen once more outside the archery range. No one has heard from her since.”

Issei averts his eyes as he reluctantly gives me the answer.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Okay. Mitsuzuri Ayako, the captain of the archery club.
We do not know where she went after returning the archery range keys, and after someone saw her in front of the archery range.”
Issei averts his gaze.

pages.ja:
授業が終わった。
例の事件の影響か、放課後の部活動は取りやめになっている。
pages.jaRuby:
授業が終わった。
例の事件の影響か、放課後の部活動は取りやめになっている。
pages.en:
Classes end.

Perhaps because of the incident, every after-school club activity has been canceled.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Classes end.
I don’t know if that incident is the reason, but all clubs are canceled for today.

pages.ja:
図書室も閉鎖されたそうで、ホームルームを終えた生徒たちは早足で校舎から去っていく。
特別な用事がない生徒は下校してください、というアナウンス。
二年Ｃ組の教室にはもう自分しかいない。
他の教室も似たような物で、急がなければ校舎はじき無人になってしまうだろう。
pages.jaRuby:
図書室も閉鎖されたそうで、ホームルームを終えた生徒たちは早足で校舎から去っていく。
特別な用事がない生徒は下校してください、というアナウンス。
二年Ｃ組の教室にはもう自分しかいない。
他の教室も似たような物で、急がなければ校舎はじき無人になってしまうだろう。
pages.en:
I hear that the library has been closed as well. The students stream from the building as soon as homeroom ends.

An announcement instructs anyone without pressing business to leave the school grounds.

I am already the only person left in Class 2-C. The other rooms must be much the same. Unless I hurry, the entire building will soon be deserted.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It seems the library is closed as well, so the students are going home in a hurry.
There’s an announcement that all students are to go home unless they have some special business.
I’m the only one left in room 2-C.
I bet it’s like this in other rooms, so I should hurry or there’ll be nobody left in the school building.

pages.ja:
「
」
その前に話を聞こう。
美綴が家に帰ってない、なんてコトを聞いて、何もせずに帰れる筈がない。
あいつはしっかりしたヤツだし、腕っ節もそんじょそこらの男より立つ。
そんなあいつが行方知れず、というのはただ事ではないし、何より友人として放っておけない。
pages.jaRuby:
「
」
その前に話を聞こう。
美綴が家に帰ってない、なんてコトを聞いて、何もせずに帰れる筈がない。
あいつはしっかりしたヤツだし、腕っ節もそんじょそこらの男より立つ。
そんなあいつが行方知れず、というのはただ事ではないし、何より友人として放っておけない。
pages.en:
“————”

Before that, I need to ask around.

I cannot hear that Mitsuzuri never returned home and simply leave without doing anything.

She is dependable, and she can hold her own against most men. For someone like her to vanish is no small matter. More importantly, she is my friend. I cannot abandon her.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
”
I should go talk to some people before that.
I can’t go straight home after I found out Mitsuzuri’s been missing.
She’s firm, and she’s stronger than most guys.
It’s not a trivial matter that she’s missing, and most of all, I can’t ignore it as her friend.

pages.ja:
「……悪いセイバー。少しやる事ができた」
セイバーに謝って、教室を後にする。
まずは二年Ａ組、美綴のクラスで話を聞いてみるべきだろう。
pages.jaRuby:
「……悪いセイバー。少しやる事ができた」
セイバーに謝って、教室を後にする。
まずは二年Ａ組、美綴のクラスで話を聞いてみるべきだろう。
pages.en:
“…Sorry, Saber. Something has come up.”

I apologize to Saber and leave the classroom.

First, I should ask around in Class 2-A, Mitsuzuri’s class.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Sorry, Saber. I have something to do.”
I apologize to Saber and leave my classroom.
I should go talk to people in Mitsuzuri’s class, room 2-A.

pages.ja:
「え？ ……あの、綾子ちゃんなら風邪でお休みしてますよ？」
「美綴なら休みだ。弓道部員ならそれぐらい知っているだろう」
「だから欠席だって。鬼の霍乱サ。あいつの無遅刻無欠席もここで終わりだやね、うひゃひゃひゃひゃひゃ」
pages.jaRuby:
「え？ ……あの、綾子ちゃんなら風邪でお休みしてますよ？」
「美綴なら休みだ。弓道部員ならそれぐらい知っているだろう」
「だから欠席だって。鬼の霍乱サ。あいつの無遅刻無欠席もここで終わりだやね、うひゃひゃひゃひゃひゃ」
pages.en:
“What? ...Um, Ayako's home with a cold, isn't she?”

“Mitsuzuri is absent. You’re in the archery club—you should know that much.”

“I told you, she's out sick. I guess even invincible Ayako catches colds. There goes her perfect attendance record! Ahahahahahaha!”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Huh? …Um, Ayako-chan is absent today because she’s sick.”
“Mitsuzuri is absent today. You should know that if you’re in the archery club.”
“I’m telling you she’s absent. Even devils get sick, huh? Her record of not being absent ends today, hahahaha.”

pages.ja:
帰り支度をしている女子の話は、決まってその程度でしかなかった。
二年Ａ組では、美綴はあくまで病欠という事になっている。
pages.jaRuby:
帰り支度をしている女子の話は、決まってその程度でしかなかった。
二年Ａ組では、美綴はあくまで病欠という事になっている。
pages.en:
Every girl still packing her things tells me some variation of the same story.

As far as Class 2-A knows, Mitsuzuri is merely absent with a cold.
pages.mirrorMoon:
That’s all I could get from the girls in her class.
It seems everyone has been told that Mitsuzuri is absent because of illness.

pages.ja:
「邪魔したな。明日美綴が来たら、このことは黙っててくれ」
片手をあげて教室を去る。
他に何かあるとしたら、もう道場ぐらいしかないのだが
pages.jaRuby:
「邪魔したな。明日美綴が来たら、このことは黙っててくれ」
片手をあげて教室を去る。
他に何かあるとしたら、もう道場ぐらいしかないのだが
pages.en:
“Sorry to bother you. If Mitsuzuri comes in tomorrow, don’t tell her I was asking around.”

I lift one hand in farewell and leave the classroom.

If there is anywhere else to look, it can only be the archery hall——
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Sorry to interrupt. Don’t tell her about this if she’s here tomorrow.”
I wave goodbye and leave.
If there’s any place to go now, it’d be the archery range.

pages.ja:
「
誰もいないか。そうだよな、部活は休みなんだから」
道場の入り口は固く閉ざされている。
中に誰かがいる様子もないし、ここにいても無意味だろう。
pages.jaRuby:
「
誰もいないか。そうだよな、部活は休みなんだから」
道場の入り口は固く閉ざされている。
中に誰かがいる様子もないし、ここにいても無意味だろう。
pages.en:
“—No one here. Of course not. Club activities were canceled.”

The doors to the archery hall are locked tight.

There is no sign of anyone inside, and no reason for me to remain here.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
No one’s here. Well, duh. There are no club activities today.”
The door to the range is shut tight.
It doesn’t seem like anyone’s inside, so it’s meaningless to stay here.

pages.ja:
「……一成に聞いてみるか。あれから何か判ったかもしれないし」
昼休みから三時間も経っているのだ。
もしかしたらとっくに美綴は見つかっていて、聞いてみればなんでもない話だった、なんて可能性もある。
pages.jaRuby:
「……一成に聞いてみるか。あれから何か判ったかもしれないし」
昼休みから三時間も経っているのだ。
もしかしたらとっくに美綴は見つかっていて、聞いてみればなんでもない話だった、なんて可能性もある。
pages.en:
“…Maybe I should ask Issei. He might have learned something since then.”

Three hours have passed since lunch.

For all I know, Mitsuzuri has already been found, and when I ask, the whole thing will turn out to have been nothing after all.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I guess I’ll talk to Issei. They might have some new information.”
It’s been three hours since lunch.
It might be possible that she’s already been found and it turned out nothing was wrong at all.
